## Status

Frozen pre-outcome SAP. No mortality status, follow-up distribution or
exposure-outcome association was examined before specification freeze. All
planned pre-outcome audits were completed before the corresponding annotated Git
tag was created.

## Primary estimand and hypothesis

The primary estimand is the adjusted prognostic hazard ratio for all-cause
mortality per doubling of baseline CRP. It is not a causal effect.

The two-sided primary hypothesis is:

```math
H_0: \beta_{\log_2(CRP)}=0
```

against:

```math
H_1: \beta_{\log_2(CRP)}\neq0
```

with `alpha = 0.05`.

## Primary analysis

- Model: survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards regression.
- Time origin: mobile examination center examination.
- Time scale: elapsed months from examination, `PERMTH_EXM`.
- Event: all-cause mortality, `MORTSTAT`.
- Exposure: `log2(CRP in mg/L)`.
- Effect measure: hazard ratio per doubling of CRP.
- Ties: Efron approximation.
- Variance: design-based robust variance.
- Survey design: MEC weight, `SDMVSTRA` and `SDMVPSU`.
- Cycle weights: `WTMEC4YR / 3` for 1999–2002 and `WTMEC2YR / 6`
  for 2003–2010.

## Eligibility

Participants must be aged 20 years or older, have positive measured CRP, have a
positive applicable MEC weight and be eligible for public mortality linkage.
Participants with confirmed pregnancy at examination will be excluded. An
indeterminate pregnancy status among participants aged 20–44 years will be
retained in the primary cohort and excluded in a sensitivity analysis. Mortality
status and follow-up time will be read only after this SAP is frozen. Final cohort
counts after special-code recoding depend on QC 03 and will be inserted before
freezing.

## Functional form

The primary CRP term is linear on the base-2 logarithmic scale. A restricted cubic
spline of `log2(CRP)` will use four knots at survey-weighted percentiles 5, 35, 65
and 95. The graphical reference will be 1 mg/L. Planned contrasts are 2, 4 and
8 mg/L versus 1 mg/L.

Age will use a restricted cubic spline with four knots at its survey-weighted
percentiles 5, 35, 65 and 95. Exposure and age knot values will be calculated and
recorded before outcome modeling.

The linear association will be assessed with a design-based Wald test. Global
spline association and nonlinearity will be assessed by joint design-based Wald
tests of the appropriate spline coefficients.

## Adjustment models

The demographic model includes age, sex, race and Hispanic origin, and survey
cycle. The primary model additionally includes educational attainment, smoking
status, body mass index, diabetes, hypertension and prevalent cardiovascular
disease. A sensitivity model additionally includes family income-to-poverty ratio.

The primary inferential result comes from the fully adjusted primary model. Models
will not be selected using univariable screening, stepwise procedures, AIC or
optimization of statistical significance.

## Missing covariates

After confirmed pregnancy exclusion, the primary eligible cohort contains 27,755
participants. The primary complete-case analysis contains 26,818 participants,
or 96.62%, after explicit recoding of numeric special-missing codes. Adding
income-to-poverty ratio reduces complete records to 24,683, or 88.93% of the
primary eligible cohort.

The sensitivity analysis will use 50 multiply imputed datasets. Predictive mean
matching is planned for continuous covariates and appropriate binary or
multinomial regression for categorical covariates. The imputation model will
include CRP, all analysis covariates, cycle, survey design variables, mortality
status and a representation of cumulative baseline hazard. CRP, mortality status,
follow-up time, weights, strata and primary sampling units will not be imputed.

The survey-weighted Cox model will be fitted within every imputed dataset.
Coefficients and design-based variances will be combined using Rubin's rules. The
implementation will be tested on outcome-blinded synthetic inputs before use.

## Proportional hazards

Proportionality will be evaluated through a survey-weighted CRP-by-log-time
interaction. Scaled Schoenfeld residual plots and covariate-specific and global
tests from an auxiliary Cox model will be supportive diagnostics.

If the CRP interaction has `p < 0.05`, or diagnostics show a sustained and
scientifically relevant temporal pattern, CRP contrasts will be reported at 5, 10
and 15 years. A constant hazard ratio will remain the principal summary only when
time-specific estimates retain the same direction and do not materially change
interpretation.

## Effect modification

Secondary models will separately test interactions between CRP and sex, and
between CRP and age group, 20–64 versus 65 years or older. Interaction contrasts
and 95% confidence intervals will be reported. No additional subgroup analysis is
pre-specified.

## Sensitivity analyses

1. Exclude deaths within 12 months.
2. Exclude deaths within 24 months.
3. Exclude CRP greater than 10 mg/L.
4. Replace below-detection CRP with 0.02 mg/dL.
5. Exclude below-detection CRP.
6. Add family income-to-poverty ratio.
7. Use multiple imputation for missing covariates.
8. Use an alternative age specification.
9. Compare weighted and unweighted estimates as a diagnostic only.
10. Exclude participants aged 20–44 years with indeterminate pregnancy status.

## Multiplicity and interpretation

There is one primary confirmatory hypothesis. Spline, interaction and sensitivity
analyses are secondary. They will be reported with estimates, confidence intervals
and p-values, but will not be treated as independent confirmatory discoveries. No
general multiplicity correction is planned.

## Outputs and diagnostics

Planned outputs include the cohort flow, weighted baseline characteristics, CRP
and `log2(CRP)` distributions, event and person-time summaries, nested-model hazard
ratios, the spline curve, proportional-hazards diagnostics, influence diagnostics,
subgroup interactions and the sensitivity-analysis table.

## Specification freeze

QC 03 has been executed and reviewed, and final pre-outcome cohort counts have
been inserted. Both documents rendered successfully and underwent final review
before the annotated specification tag. Any subsequent change must be documented
prospectively as a numbered amendment.
